final:
Composite CDS units with more than one `/` now parse correctly. `10+3J/m/s/kpc2` reads as `1000 J / (kpc2 m s)`, and `10-7J/s/kpc2` reads as `1e-07 J / (kpc2 s)`. I ran the CDS unit tests and the ascii CDS reader tests (757 passed). I did not run `Table.read` on your example file itself, only the unit parser it uses.

**Cause:** The CDS unit grammar in `astropy/units/format/cds.py` grouped divisions from the right. So `a/b/c` was read as `a/(b/c)`, which is why the `s` and `kpc2` ended up in the wrong place.

**Fix:**
- **Grammar:** I changed the division rule in `astropy/units/format/cds.py` to group from the left, so `a/b/c` is `(a/b)/c`.
- **Parser table:** `astropy/units/format/cds_parsetab.py` is a pre-generated, tracked file, and it was stale after the grammar change. I deleted it and let it regenerate, so it shows as modified in the diff.
- **Tests:** I added three cases to `test_cds_grammar` in `astropy/units/tests/test_format.py`: `J/m/s/kpc2`, `10+3J/m/s/kpc2` and `10-7J/s/kpc2`.

I also checked `m.s/kpc2`, a leading `/m` and `km/s/Mpc` (now `km / (Mpc s)`). All parse as expected.

The rehearsal log is in `.rehearsal/REHEARSAL.md`; I left `.rehearsal/` in place.
